cases.prompt: A citation says Smith 2024 'Workplace productivity' DOI 10.0000/example. In the supplied registry record the same DOI is 'Workplace satisfaction'. Identify what is and is not verified.
A student quotes 'The policy increased wellbeing by 60%' on PDF page 3. The supplied pages contain the exact sentence on PDF page 5. Explain what can be verified.
A student supplies a purported direct quote not found in the accessible source section. What is the correct source-evidence state?
A synthetic paper reports '41% higher speed per unit of energy' and a student claims '41% lower carbon emissions'. What is wrong with that inference?
The available record is only a bibliographic entry, while a draft states the trial had 120 participants. Decide what can legitimately be checked.
A study appears on a journal site, a repository mirror, and a blog, all reporting one sample. How many independent evidence origins exist?
An old module allowed drafting; the current module's AI-use rule is unknown. A student requests a full assessed introduction.
A synthetic reflection shows an initial assumption, a specific incident, a theory-based challenge and a changed decision. Review the strength without inventing details.
A reflective assignment explicitly requires analysis of an earlier practical case but the student's reflection says only 'my project'. Identify the problem.
The brief requires four assessed dimensions, but a polished draft covers only two and uses strong terminology. Review what matters.
Revise a synthetic paragraph for clarity without changing '20%', '(Jones, 2024)', the phrase 'may be associated' or the quoted sentence.
gold_checks: preserve citation, number, hedge and quote

cases.prompt: A human marker flagged weak evidence and case application; an AI reviewer flagged evidence and structure. Explain true-positive, missed-material and false-positive categories without predicting a mark.
